So the default start supports plain HTML or vite. Plain HTML is simplest, no dependencies, works with static deployment. I'll build a polished single-page game with pure HTML/CSS/JS (ES modules), canvas-based isometric-ish top-down retro pixel art, with:

- Grid map (tile-based, e.g. 24x18)
- Buildings: Lumberjack hut (wood), Stone quarry (stone), Storehouse (capacity + storage), maybe Farm/food, House (population/workers). The prompt requires lumberjack hut, stone quarry, storehouse. Add house for expansion, and maybe roads?
- Automated resource collection: workers/loggers walk from hut to nearby trees and back, quarry workers mine rock, deposit into storehouses.
- Economy loop: spend wood+stone to build; buildings need workers; population grows; storehouse capacity limits; maybe tools/food.
- Expand settlement: unlock/build more, terrain, fog of war? Keep manageable.
- Retro top-down 2D with pixel art drawn procedurally on canvas (no external assets to keep it self-contained).
- Mobile support per Agents.md: responsive, touch controls.

Need to "finish the game" — a complete, polished, playable experience with win condition / progression, tutorial, sound maybe via WebAudio, save/load localStorage, speed controls, pause, build menu, tooltips, notifications.

Let me plan architecture:

Files:
- index.html
- styles.css
- js/main.js (bootstrap, game loop, input)
- js/state.js maybe
- js/world.js (grid, terrain generation, resource nodes)
- js/buildings.js (definitions)
- js/workers.js (agent AI, pathfinding maybe simple)
- js/render.js (isometric-ish top-down renderer with pixel art)
- js/ui.js (HUD, build menu, tooltips)
- js/audio.js (procedural sfx)

Could be one big JS for simplicity, but modular is nicer. Keep ~1500-2500 lines total.

Game design details:

Map: 28 x 20 tiles. Tile size dynamically fit. Top-down 2D, slight 3/4 perspective drawn sprites? "2D top-down retro" — I'll do top-down with subtle fake-3D building sprites (roof shown). Retro pixel palette, chunky pixels, scanline/vignette optional. Pixel art drawn in code per building via canvas primitives. Use an offscreen canvas sprite cache at low resolution (e.g. tile 16px logical) scaled up with imageSmoothingEnabled false for authentic pixel look. Better: render game at logical resolution (~480x320 equivalent or tile 24 px logical) to offscreen canvas then upscale. But UI is DOM. Gameplay canvas scaled.

I'll design tile size 32 logical px? Map 30x22 at 32 = 960x704, scale to fit. For retro, render sprites at 16px logical and scale x2. Let's use TILE=32 world units, draw pixel art with 2px "pixels" (i.e., 16x16 sprite at 2x). Simpler: draw all art procedurally at 16x16 unit sprites and scale 2, tile=32. Terrain via 16x16 patterns at scale 2.

Camera: fixed whole map if fits? 30x22 at 32 = 960x704. Larger than mobile. Implement camera pan/zoom? Complexity. Alternative: map 26x18 = 832x576, camera fits desktop nicely, on mobile pan/zoom with touch. Could implement camera with drag and pinch, plus auto clamp. Reasonable.

Better: world canvas container occupies full screen under HUD; camera centered on map and scale computed to fit min dimension; allow zoom in/out and drag. This is doable.

Let me simplify rendering: top-down, tile map with grass variants, forests (tree clusters), rock outcrops, water pond, paths. Resource nodes: trees (wood) and rock (stone) with quantity. Lumberjack hut places lumberjack workers; quarry places miners. Workers physically travel from building to nearest resource node, harvest for some seconds, carry back, deposit to nearest storehouse (or own building storage). Storehouse central storage capacity shared? In Settlers, goods stored in buildings. Simplify: global resources with caps determined by storehouses (e.g., base 100 each, each storehouse +150). But visual workers deposit into storehouses. If no storehouse, deposit into the producing building (which holds small buffer) — actually start with a storehouse prebuilt so it's intuitive. Start: storehouse + small starting resources. Tutorial tasks: build lumberjack hut, build quarry, build house, reach population 12, etc.

Economy:
- Resources: wood, stone, plus maybe "tools" crafted at workshop for upgrades? Keep scope: wood, stone, food? Prompt only says wood, stone. Add "settlers" population as resource. Maybe add coins/tax for flavor? Keep wood/stone and population; building costs; storehouse capacity.
- Buildings:
  - Lumberjack hut: cost 20 wood; produces wood via worker; needs 1 worker; trees nearby speed.
  - Stone quarry: cost 20 wood + 10 stone; must be placed on/near rock; produces stone; 1 worker.
  - Storehouse: cost 30 wood + 20 stone; +200 capacity each; allows deposit; 0 workers.
  - House: cost 25 wood + 10 stone; +2 population capacity and spawns settlers; increases worker pool.
  - Well/farm? maybe "Farm" cost 20 wood produces food, needed to grow? That adds complexity but nice loop. Prompt says simple economy loop. I'll add Farm optional? Hmm, to finish and polish, add "Farm" that produces food; population consumes food; if food runs out, production slows. That's a real loop. But prompt explicitly features wood/stone, "simple economy loop" and expand settlement. Adding food consumption can frustrate. Maybe add Farm that produces food used to grow population (houses need food to spawn). Simpler: population grows automatically from houses over time; houses need wood/stone to build. Food not needed. Keep wood+stone+people. Add decorative windmill? Scope control.

I'll do 5 building types: Storehouse, Lumberjack Hut, Quarry, House, plus Watchtower? No combat requested. Maybe "Workshop" to upgrade tools, increasing gather rate; adds progression sink. And "Town Hall" as win condition: build monument/town hall costing 150 wood 120 stone, requires pop 10, wins game. That gives goal and expansion. Add "Market"? no.

Let's include:
1. Storehouse (storage +200 each, deposit point)
2. Lumberjack Hut (wood production)
3. Stone Quarry (stone production, requires rock tiles adjacent? place near rock)
4. House (+2 pop capacity, enables new workers)
5. Workshop (upgrade gathering: +25% per workshop? global tool upgrade levels). Could be "Toolsmith": each one adds +15% harvest speed.
6. Town Hall (win condition, big cost, requires population >= 12). Unlock after houses maybe.

Workers:
- Population capacity from start 4? Start with 4 settlers, storehouse, some resources (50 wood, 30 stone), and a lumberjack hut? Tutorial asks player to build first hut. Start with storehouse and 4 settlers, 60 wood, 20 stone maybe.
- Each production building requires 1 worker. Assignment automatically: idle settlers get assigned to unstaffed building nearest? UI shows workers. Automate to keep simple: buildings auto-staff when population available. Workers are simulated agents walking.
- Population grows when food? Let's do: Houses spawn a new settler every 20 seconds if there's spare capacity and resources? Free population. Population cap = 3 (start) +2 per house. New settlers arrive over time (every 12s per house?) as long as pop < cap and at least ... no cost. That makes building houses useful. If pop cap increases, new settlers walk in from map edge. Nice.
- Workers carry 1-3 units per trip. Harvest time based on distance and tool upgrades. Trees have regrowth: after chopped, tree stump regrows in 60s. Rocks infinite but slower? Quarries often built on stone deposits which deplete. Use rock nodes with large reserves (e.g., 40) that deplete and disappear, forcing expansion. Trees respawn.

Production loop AI:
State machine per worker: idle -> goToResource -> harvest (timer) -> return to storehouse -> deposit -> repeat. Pathfinding: straight-line movement with simple obstacle avoidance? Grid A* would be robust. Buildings occupy tiles; trees/rocks occupy tiles. A* on grid, max ~600 tiles, fine. Simple 4/8-direction A* with diagonal movement. Cache paths occasionally. Or simpler: workers move in straight lines and can walk through resources/buildings (visual overlap fine?) That looks poor. Implement A*: it's not hard, ~80 lines. Workers walk on empty tiles; building tiles blocked; resource tiles blocked except target adjacency. Use 8-dir with no corner cutting.

- Terrain layer pre-rendered to offscreen canvas at full map resolution for performance.
- Trees/rocks drawn each frame from state with sprites.
- Buildings drawn with generated pixel sprites; construction animation (scaffold) over 3-5s after placement? Nice.
- Workers small 8x8 pixel dudes with hats, carrying icons.
